item.content:encoded:
The sun came up and another massive opportunity awaits Indiana.

The Hoosiers arrive at Michigan seeking their second-straight win over the Wolverines, and their first win in Ann Arbor since 1967.

Here’s everything you need to know about Indiana’s week 8 matchup against Michigan.

No. 6 INDIANA HOOSIERS (6-1) at MICHIGAN WOLVERINES (4-2)

  • Kickoff:  Noon ET, Saturday
  • Location:  Ann Arbor, Michigan; Michigan Stadium (107,601)
  • Television:  FOX — Gus Johnson (pbp), Joel Klatt (color) & Jenny Taft (sideline)
  • Stream:  FOX Sports
  • Radio:  IU Football radio network
  • Odds:  Indiana is around a 7.5-point favorite
  • Weather at kickoff:  58 degrees, sunny, wind 4 mph, 0% chance of precipitation.
  • Series:  Michigan leads the all-time series 62-11.  IU won last meeting 20-15 in 2024.
  • Tickets:  SOLD OUT.  Use our StubHub affiliate link
  • The Coaches:
    • Curt Cignetti is in his third year as the head coach at IU.  He holds a 152-38 record in his 16th season as a college head coach.  He’s 33-3 at Indiana.
    • Kyle Whittingham is the head coach of Michigan.  He’s in his first year at Michigan and 181-90 as a head coach.

The sun comes up tomorrow & we get to compete. https://t.co/9rpclEmYE6

— Indiana Football (@IndianaFootball) October 24, 2026

GAMEDAY TIMELINE

THE COMPLETE BIG TEN WEEK 8 SLATE

Saturday, October 24

  • Indiana at Michigan — 12 p.m., FOX
  • Rutgers at Northwestern — 12 p.m., Peacock
  • Oregon at Illinois — 3 p.m., Big Ten Network
  • Michigan State at UCLA — 3:30 p.m., CBS
  • Iowa at Minnesota — 3:30 p.m., FS1
  • USC at Wisconsin — 7:30 p.m., NBC / Peacock

TALE OF THE TAPE 

AVAILABILITY REPORT

MICHIGAN RESULTS

Date Time At Opponent Location Result
Sep 5 (Sat) 7:30 PM Home Western Michigan Ann Arbor, Mich. W 13-12
Sep 12 (Sat) Noon Home #11 Oklahoma Ann Arbor, Mich. W 17-10
Sep 19 (Sat) 3:30 PM Home UTEP Ann Arbor, Mich. W 52-17
Sep 26 (Sat) 3:30 PM Home #17 Iowa Ann Arbor, Mich. L 19-20
Oct 3 (Sat) 11:00 AM CT Away Minnesota Minneapolis, Minn. L 14-20
Oct 17 (Sat) 3:30 PM Home Penn State Ann Arbor, Mich. W 21-18

MICHIGAN NOTES AND NUMBERS

(Via Michigan Athletics)

MATCHUP

  • Michigan’s .849 winning percentage against Indiana is the program’s highest against any conference opponent.
  • Michigan holds a 36-7 all-time record against Indiana at Michigan Stadium.
  • The Wolverines have won 22 straight home games against the Hoosiers, including a 52-7 victory in 2023.
  • Indiana’s last win at Michigan Stadium was a 27-20 victory in 1967.

MICHIGAN OFFENSE

  • The U-M offense came alive after halftime against Penn State, totaling 21 points and 221 yards (174 rushing) in the second half while averaging 7.4 yards per play.
  • Michigan has recorded 100 first downs this season — 46 rushing, 45 passing and nine by penalty.
  • While the Wolverines are working to improve their third-down conversion rate of 40.8 percent (29-for-71), the offense has converted 71.4 percent of its fourth-down attempts (5-for-7), ranking 19th nationally.
  • Michigan’s offense is seeking greater consistency and balance in explosive plays (20-plus yards). The offense has generated 16, including 12 through the passing game. Against Penn State, U-M broke through with three explosive rushing plays.
  • The passing game has produced four touchdowns on explosive plays, including three connections between quarterback Bryce Underwood and wide receiver JJ Buchanan.
  • JJ Buchanan (seven) and Andrew Marsh (four) lead the team in explosive offensive plays, all on receptions. Marsh led U-M in 2025 with 15 explosive plays on offense (14 receiving, one rushing) and another eight on special teams returns.
  • Jordan Marshall leads the team with four rushing touchdowns, while JJ Buchanan has a team-high four receiving touchdowns.
  • U-M has two receivers who have combined for four 100-yard games this season: JJ Buchanan (126 vs. Western Michigan, 130 vs. Iowa) and Andrew Marsh (105 vs. UTEP, 106 vs. Iowa).
  • Against Penn State, U-M recorded multiple explosive runs in a game for the first time this season. Runs of 43 yards (Bryson Kuzdzal, touchdown), 22 yards (Tommy Carr) and 41 yards (Savion Hiter) were three of Michigan’s four longest rushes this season, along with a 38-yard touchdown run by Bryce Underwood.
  • The offensive line continues to develop. Four players have made double-digit starts at Michigan: left guard/tackle Evan Link (23 starts, 22 at tackle), right tackle Andrew Sprague (15), center Jake Guarnera (16, including 10 at guard) and tackle Blake Frazier (14, including four at right tackle).
  • The unit helped produce Michigan’s best rushing performance of the season against Penn State (211 yards), its first game with more than 200 rushing yards since Nov. 22, 2025, at Maryland.
  • The offensive line allows an average of 4.0 tackles for loss per game, ranking 31st nationally, and has used four different starting combinations through six games.
  • The running game has improved as games progress. U-M averages 5.07 yards per carry in the second half, and 14 of its 19 runs of 10-plus yards have come after halftime.
  • Quarterback Tommy Carr saw his first extended action against Penn State, playing the entire second half. Carr completed five of seven passes for 47 yards and scored on a 12-yard touchdown run, leading three touchdown drives in the comeback win.

MICHIGAN DEFENSE

  • Michigan forced three turnovers against Penn State (two interceptions and a strip sack), its third game with multiple takeaways this season (also Oklahoma and Minnesota).
  • Through six games, U-M has allowed 10 touchdowns and ranks 21st nationally in scoring defense (16.2 points per game). No opponent has scored more than 14 points in a half against Michigan this season.
  • The defense ranks 25th nationally in tackles for loss per game (6.5), led by John Henry Daley with 6.0.
  • Daley also leads the team with 4.0 sacks. Eleven different players have recorded at least a share of a sack this season.
  • Michigan ranks 14th nationally in passing defense, allowing 166.8 yards per game. Opposing passers have thrown seven touchdowns and six interceptions.
  • The rush defense has held opponents below 100 yards three times, allowing 89.7 yards per game (13th nationally). Minnesota and Penn State are the only teams to score rushing touchdowns against U-M this season, though the Nittany Lions were limited to 65 rushing yards.
  • The defense has forced eight turnovers in six games, including six interceptions, two of which were returned for touchdowns. U-M is one of six teams nationally with multiple defensive touchdowns.

MICHIGAN SPECIAL TEAMS

  • Kicker Trey Butkowski made 19 of 22 field-goal attempts in his lone season at Pitt after joining the team as a walk-on. He is 4-for-4 this season.
  • Punter Cam Brown averaged 43.9 yards on 22 punts during his freshman season at Utah and has averaged 41.9 yards per punt this season.
  • Brown has punted 30 times this season, placing 13 inside the 20-yard line. He has forced 13 fair catches and had two punts downed at the 1-yard line against Oklahoma, when he pinned the Sooners inside their 20 on six of seven attempts.
  • Kickoff specialist Jacob Baggett has recorded 17 touchbacks on 26 kickoffs.
  • U-M is one of eight teams nationally to have blocked or tipped multiple punts.
  • Freshman Salesi Moa made his debut as Michigan’s punt returner against Penn State, recording two fair catches and one return for nine yards.

MORE MICHIGAN WEEK COVERAGE

  • Notes, numbers and key matchups for IU football’s Saturday matchup at Michigan
  • Radio show: IU football coach Curt Cignetti recaps OSU game, previews Michigan
  • IU football has no one on injury report for Michigan, including Khobie Martin
  • Reports: Michigan is going with Tommy Carr as starting QB vs. IU
  • Winning at the Big House has been a big challenge for IU football
  • Watch: Q&As with IU football’s Tyrique Tucker and Charlie Becker — Michigan week
  • Here’s how Curt Cignetti’s teams have performed following a loss
  • IU football notebook: The sun came up and Curt Cignetti has a new perspective
  • Watch: IU football coach Curt Cignetti Monday Q&A — Michigan week

PREDICTIONS

Indiana’s in for a third straight Big Ten slog.

You know the routine by now.  With it’s young but mobile quarterback, Michigan will try to shorten the game with the running game, roll outs and quick hitters that lead to long drives.

While the game follows Michigan’s script, the Hoosiers do just enough.

TDH PREDICTION:  INDIANA 20 MICHIGAN 13

  • ESPN SP+ (Computer):  Indiana 26 Michigan 18 (69% win probability for IU)
  • ESPN FPI (Computer):  Indiana has a 82.2% chance to win.

item.content:encoded:
How does IU basketball compare in 2026 when it comes to its resources available to pay players?

CBS Sports says it contacted more than 100 sources to dive deep into what NIL looks like in college basketball this season.

But we before we go any further — we interrupt this article with caveats.

All attempts to estimate school-by-school spending on revenue sharing and name, image and likeness should be met with a high degree of skepticism.

Because no one outside the programs know the details with any real measure of precision.  So whether it’s one source, 100 or 1,000, what CBS has compiled can at best be called a directional indicator, or a swag (sophisticated wild-ass guess) if you prefer.

But this is at least better than what we see often — some random social media account using AI to cobble together slop.

CBS says 11 men’s college basketball programs are projected to spend more than $20 million on their rosters during the 2026-27 campaign — Texas Tech, Kentucky, Illinois, Texas, Florida, St. John’s, Louisville, Duke, Tennessee, North Carolina and Michigan.

Indiana is one of four schools CBS says is in Tier 2 at “just under $20 million,” along with UConn, Arkansas, and Kansas.

For IU, this does seems directionally correct based on what we know about Indiana’s roster and spending habits.  Is it $17, 18 or 19 million?  Nobody on the outside really knows that — and for that matter — very few on the inside know.  Schools don’t want the details to get out, so the information is closely guarded.

To this point, IU hasn’t been getting a strong return on its player investments.  And ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, CBS suggests Indiana has overspent relative to its preseason standing.

“Indiana was a big spender ahead of a big second season for Darian DeVries, but despite many a Big Ten foe believing otherwise, IU did not hit the $20 million mark,” the report says.  “Will the investment pay off with a team worthy of Top 25 status more weeks than not this season? The Hoosiers are one of only two teams that comfortably rank in the top 15 in spending but are not ranked in the preseason AP Top 25. (North Carolina, under a first-year coach, is the other.)”

CBS says the average cost of a Big Ten roster is $12.7 million.  Michigan and Illinois are the lone schools ahead of Indiana.  They’re both in the north of $20 million first tier.

You have to go all the way down to Tier 6, at $7-9.9 million to find Purdue.  They’re there with Penn State, Northwestern, Rutgers and Iowa as the lowest-budget teams in the Big Ten.

item.content:encoded:
IU basketball is getting a visit from class of 2028 4-star wing Isaac Smith next month.

He’ll visit Bloomington starting on Nov. 13, national 247Sports analyst Eric Bossi reported on X.

IU football hosts USC that weekend.

Indiana offered Smith a few months ago.

From Virginia, Smith attends Monarch Academy in Kansas City, Kansas.  The IU staff has deep ties in both locations.

The 6-foot-6 Smith is a 4-star, the No. 34 overall player, and the No. 11 small forward in the composite rankings.

Smith is a classic wing, with length, athleticism and the ability to both shoot from the perimeter and score off the bounce.

As a sophomore, Smith attended Hargrave Military Academy, where he averaged 17.8 points, 6.7 rebounds and 2.1 assists per contest.

For travel basketball Smith played for Team United on the Nike EYBL Circuit.  He is averaging 12.8 points, 2.9 assists, and 1.4 steals while shooting 39.1 percent from three in those contests.

In addition to IU, Smith has offers from Kansas, Michigan, Cincinnati, Arizona State, Vanderbilt, West Virginia, Texas Tech, Virginia Tech, Virginia, Georgetown, Texas A&M, Oklahoma State, N.C. State, and Mississippi State.

Indiana currently has no commits early in the 2028 cycle.

item.title: Michigan DT coach Larry Black to face his alma mater on Saturday
item.dc:creator: Mike Schumann
item.description: Saturday’s game means a little bit more to Michigan defensive tackles coach Larry Black. As an Ohio native, you might expect facing Ohio State in the end of season rivalry matchup will stir up some emotions for the first-year Michigan assistant. But first there’s the matter of going up against his alma mater for the [...]
item.content:encoded:
Saturday’s game means a little bit more to Michigan defensive tackles coach Larry Black.

As an Ohio native, you might expect facing Ohio State in the end of season rivalry matchup will stir up some emotions for the first-year Michigan assistant.

But first there’s the matter of going up against his alma mater for the first time in his 12 years as an assistant coach.

Black was a four-year starter for Indiana from 2009-12.  While there weren’t any memorable seasons during his time at IU playing for Bill Lynch and Kevin Wilson, he was a highly productive defensive tackle.

He finished his career with 127 tackles, 55 solo, with eight sacks (51 yards), 27.5 tackles for loss (100 yards), two fumble recoveries, four pass breakups and one blocked field goal. He started 40 games and appeared in all 48 of Indiana’s games over his career.

And there were memorable moments — including against Michigan.

Black started and had two tackles for loss against the Wolverines in 2009, the infamous Bill Lynch gum-toss game when the Hoosiers lost to No. 23 Michigan 36-33 in Ann Arbor.  He also played against Michigan in 2010, another heartbreaker for the Hoosiers, who fell 42-35.

One thing Black never saw was Indiana favored against Michigan going into a game like it is this weekend, or the Hoosiers pull off a win over UM like they’ve done twice in the last six years.

Black’s phone is blowing up this week.  His former IU teammates are feeling confident.

“I got like 20 teammates who were texting me,” Black said.  “We’ll get with them here soon.”

The dynamics of Indiana vs. Michigan have changed dramatically since Black was a Hoosier.

“Playing at IU, being able to go against them on Saturday. I was telling the D-Line the other day, you got the national champs coming in here, so like what what better opportunity do you want?

“But it’s cool, man.  I met my wife there. Like, that’s been a big part, but I’m at Michigan and it’s good to be on this side and it’s an exciting opportunity to go get after those guys.”

Black graduated from IU with a bachelor of science degree in recreational sport management in December 2012.  He signed as a free agent with the Cincinnati Bengals and he’s had coaching stops at Carthage, Toledo, Notre Dame and Vanderbilt prior to arriving in Ann Arbor this year.

item.title: Notes, numbers and key matchups for IU football’s Saturday matchup at Michigan
item.dc:creator: Jack Rizzo
item.description: No. 6 IU football suffered its first home loss in the Curt Cignetti era last Saturday to Ohio State, 19-15. The loss dropped the Hoosiers record to 6-1 on the season. The loss also snapped Indiana’s 22-game winning streak, which was the longest running streak in the nation. IU now has a record of 33-3 [...]
item.content:encoded:
No. 6 IU football suffered its first home loss in the Curt Cignetti era last Saturday to Ohio State, 19-15. The loss dropped the Hoosiers record to 6-1 on the season.

The loss also snapped Indiana’s 22-game winning streak, which was the longest running streak in the nation. IU now has a record of 33-3 under Cignetti.

The Hoosiers will turn their attention to the Michigan Wolverines, who are coming off a bounce back win over Penn State. The game will be played in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Kickoff is scheduled for noon Eastern and will be televised on FOX.

Here are some notes, numbers and key matchups to know before the game kicks off at Michigan Stadium.

_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _

NOTES

  • Michigan leads the all time series over Indiana, 62-11. IU won the last matchup in 2024 at Memorial Stadium. The last time the two teams played in Ann Arbor was in 2023, a 52-7 victory for the Wolverines. The Hoosiers have not won at Michigan Stadium since 1967, when IU beat Michigan 27-20.
  • IU quarterback Josh Hoover has 18 touchdown passes to zero interceptions this season. He is one of just two quarterbacks since 2010 to have 15 or more touchdowns and zero interceptions through the first seven games, joining Marcus Mariota, who did it in his Heisman season back in 2014.
  • True freshman Tommy Carr took over for a struggling Bryce Underwood in Michigan’s 21-18 victory over Penn State last week.  On the season in two games Carr is 7-for-9 passing for 70 yards and a touchdown, while adding 54 yards and a score on the ground. Carr will make his first collegiate start against the Hoosiers this week.
  • Saturday’s game will be IU’s third road contest in the month of October. The Hoosiers have already picked up road wins over Rutgers and Nebraska. Under Cignetti, Indiana is 10-2 in true road games, with both losses coming to national top-10 programs (Ohio State, Notre Dame).
  • For the third consecutive week, the Hoosiers play at noon Eastern on FOX. Big Noon Kickoff will be live from Ann Arbor, as it was in Lincoln for Nebraska and Bloomington for Ohio State. Five of IU’s eight games this season have been televised on FOX.
  • Michigan Stadium has the largest capacity of any American football stadium in the world, seating well over 107,000 spectators for each home game. The Hoosiers have already been challenged by 85,000 screaming fans at Nebraska’s Memorial Stadium, and Saturday’s game will be no exception.

NUMBERS

  • 7 – IU’s seven-straight road victories is the longest active streak of any Power 4 team, along with the second longest streak in the FBS.
  • 10 – Amare Ferrell’s two interceptions against Ohio State give the safety 10 for his career, placing him in a tie for sixth all-time in program history. John McDonnell and Eric Allen also had 10 career interceptions at IU.
  • 30 – Nick Marsh has now recorded at least one reception in 30 consecutive games to begin his college career. That includes 29 games in a row with multiple receptions for the Michigan State transfer.
  • 100 – Indiana has now had three-straight games with a 100-yard receiver. Charlie Becker posted a career-high 165 receiving yards against Ohio State.
  • 131 – The combined age of the two head coaches in this matchup, Curt Cignetti (65) and Kyle Whittingham (66). The two coaches have more than 80 years of coaching experience combined.

KEY MATCHUPS

  • Tommy Carr vs. IU pass rush – Carr provided a much-needed spark for the Michigan offense last week, making play-after-play with both his arm and legs. The Indiana front has struggled to contain mobile quarterbacks this season, such as Aidan Chiles (Northwestern) and Anthony Colandrea (Nebraska). The Hoosiers must force Carr to make plays in the pocket.
  • IU pass game vs. Michigan secondary – The Hoosiers’ passing attack puts an emphasis on big plays, especially throws down the field to Charlie Becker. However, Josh Hoover is going up against a stingy Michigan secondary that only allows 166.8 passing yards per game, good for third-best in the Big Ten.
  • Curt Cignetti vs. Kyle Whittingham – Two of the most successful collegiate head coaches this century will square off on Saturday. Both coaches are known for their intense style, and getting the most out of their rosters. Over eight decades of experience will be going head-to-head on Saturday.
  • IU vs. Michigan crowd – During practice this week, IU practiced with crowd noise in preparation for the more than 100,000 screaming Michigan fans expected in attendance. The Hoosiers also practiced with crowd noise prior to Nebraska. Once again, Indiana will likely have to resort to a silent count on Saturday.

A product of Naperville, Illinois, Kelly attends Neuqua Valley H.S.  As a sophomore he averaged 19.6 points, 7.6 rebounds and [...]
item.content:encoded:
Class of 2028 wing Cole Kelly announced an offer from IU basketball on Thursday.

The 6-foot-6 lefty recently took a visit to Bloomington and received the offer during a conversation with head coach Darian DeVries.

A product of Naperville, Illinois, Kelly attends Neuqua Valley H.S.  As a sophomore he averaged 19.6 points, 7.6 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game, earned first-team All-State and was named the DuPage Valley Conference Player of the Year.  He made 51% of his shots from the floor and knocked down more than 70 three-pointers.

In the average of the national rankings, Kelly is a 4-star, the No. 32 overall player in the class, and the No. 8 small forward.

Kelly has a complete game.  He’s a skilled wing who can handle the ball, score inside and out, and plays with the toughness and physicality of a big man.

For travel basketball, Kelly plays for Breakaway Basketball on the Adidas 3SSB Circuit.  Playing with the 17u class he averaged 16.8 points, 7.8 rebounds and 5.4 assists while making 2.5 threes per game.

In addition to Indiana, Kelly has offers from Iowa, Nebraska, Missouri, Wisconsin, Illinois, Purdue, Ohio State, Creighton, Northwestern, Notre Dame, Butler, Marquette and others.

Cooper flashed in his first game back after sustaining an ankle injury in Week 1 that put him on the reserved/injured list. Cooper averaged [...]
item.content:encoded:
After returning to action against the Patriots and leading the Jets with 6 receptions, 103 receiving yards and a TD, Omar Cooper Jr. was named the Pepsi Rookie of the Week. Cooper flashed in his first game back after sustaining an ankle injury in Week 1 that put him on the reserved/injured list.

Cooper averaged 17.2 yards per reception, becoming the fifth Jets rookie to average 15-plus yards per catch in a single game in the last 10 seasons, according to Stats Perform.

Meanwhile, former IU linebacker Aiden Fisher was released by the Houston Texans and signed to the Kansas City Chiefs’ practice squad.  He joins former IU teammate Kahlil Benson in Kansas City.  After being drafted by Houston in the seventh round, Fisher played in three games for the Texans and posted one tackle.

From 2024-25 at Indiana, Fisher totaled 215 tackles, including 16 for a loss and six sacks. Fisher’s production led to him being named a two-time first-team All-American and two-time first-team All-Big Ten selection.

In same news cycle the Chiefs waived former IU linebacker Cam Jones.

FOUR ON SEASON OPENING NBA ROSTERS

Four former IU basketball players were on opening day NBA rosters this week.

OG Anunoby is with the Knicks, Thomas Bryant is with Cleveland, Trayce Jackson-Davis is with Toronto, and Kel’el Ware is with Milwaukee.

item.title: An encouraging sign: IU basketball “manhandling” opponents on the glass
item.dc:creator: Mike Schumann
item.description: When it comes to priority No. 1 during the offseason, Indiana basketball is two-for-two. The Hoosiers outrebounded Butler 53-33 at Hinkle Fieldhouse earlier this month, and they followed that up by posting an even larger 53-31 margin against North Carolina at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Sunday. IU had 17 offensive rebounds against Butler, and then 20 [...]
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to priority No. 1 during the offseason, Indiana basketball is two-for-two.

The Hoosiers outrebounded Butler 53-33 at Hinkle Fieldhouse earlier this month, and they followed that up by posting an even larger 53-31 margin against North Carolina at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Sunday.

IU had 17 offensive rebounds against Butler, and then 20 against the Tar Heels, and produced a total of 42 second chance points in the two games it won by a combined score of 46.

North Carolina coach Michael Malone was frustrated by the way Indiana dominated his team on the boards.

“To be manhandled, to be outworked on the glass was disappointing,” he said after Indiana’s 76-58 win.

Even in exhibitions, the rebounding numbers are eye-popping against fellow high majors, and to put those early results in context, consider this: IU was outrebounded by a total of 121 in its 14 losses last season, or 8.6 per game.  In some of the losses the margin was massive, including -18 at Michigan, -17 at Michigan State, -15 at USC, and -14 at Purdue, Minnesota and Illinois.

IU only got double-digit offensive rebounds once last season against a high major opponent — and that was 12 at a an undersized Maryland team.

As his debut season in Bloomington wound towards its end, IU coach Darian DeVries began to acknowledge he felt a lack of size played a role in those 14 losses that caused the Hoosiers to miss the NCAA Tournament.  He plugged in two bigs as starters for the first time all season at the Big Ten Tournament, but it was too little too late by that point.

DeVries could not ignore that some of the top teams in the nation last year were top-10 nationally in rebounding margin, including Michigan, Michigan State, Illinois, Florida, Tennessee, Duke, and Arizona.  Five of the top-10 teams in rebounding margin made the Elite Eight of the NCAA Tournament, and three made the Final Four.

You either match that size, or you get overwhelmed.

So with another roster rebuild ahead of them, IU went about placing a heavy emphasis on the glass.

“It’s been our focus the whole offseason,” DeVries said after the Butler exhibition.  “We want to be built for that.”

IU added the tallest player in program history in 7-foot-2 Samet Yigitoglu.  He’s proving to be more nimble than you might expect for his massive frame.  He can rebound over people, of course, but he’ll also move out of his area and tap an offensive rebound out to a guard.

The Hoosiers have never had a 7-foot power forward until this year either, but that’s how the program lists Aiden Sherrell.  When he’s at the four, Sherrell is going to have a size advantage in just about every matchup he’s in too.

Through two games, again, against high major length and athleticism, the results are notable.

Sherrell is averaging 9.5 rebounds including 3.5 on the offensive glass, and Yigitoglu has posted 8.0 and 3.5.  Coming off the bench to bolster that duo is Sam Alexis, who has averaged 11.8 rebounds per-40 minutes over his college career.

But DeVries’ focus on rebounding appears to extend beyond his big men.  The second-year IU coach had to decide on whether to start Jaeden Mustaf or Bryce Lindsay ahead of the exhibitions.  They were both high major starters a year ago, and as Lindsay’s 26 points off the bench against North Carolina highlighted, it was no easy choice.

Part of the decision was the size, defensive presence, physicality, and yes, rebounding ability Mustaf provides.  The 6-foot-6 wing has averaged 6.5 rebounds including 2.0 on the offensive end in the exhibitions.

As you may have noted, those massive rebounding deficits a year ago were all on the road.  That’s where often shots don’t fall and turnovers pile up.  Indiana saw that dynamic play out against North Carolina on Sunday when it shot 36% and coughed it up 15 times.  Those are losing numbers on most nights.

Unless of course, you rebound 20 of your own misses and score 17 second chance points.

“We weren’t very clean on the offensive end, but we were still able to overcome it with some offensive rebounding,” DeVries said Sunday.  “And like I told them before the game, we’ve been talking about it all summer and fall, this is our identity. This is who we’re going to be. Just embrace it because we’re going to stay on it, stay on it, stay on it. And again, I thought that eventually broke the game open.”

Of course a heavy emphasis on offensive rebounding comes with potential risks when you come up empty.

The more players crashing the offensive glass means less players back in transition.

That’s an area of focus, especially as this Indiana team gets scouted more and more.

“Occasionally you are going to get caught a little bit, maybe with some long rebounds, and maybe it leads to some breakouts,” DeVries said.  “So, your transition from going to the glass to getting your defense put back together is a huge priority.

“But I think it’s going to be worth the risk for us, because those second and third opportunities, you score at such a high rate when you get an offensive rebound, whether you just get a putback or a kickout three, that we just feel like if we can get enough quality shots on our first attempt, but then on the ones we do miss, if we can get second and third opportunities, it has a chance to make us an elite offense.”
